hypotheses.title: Oridonin Extends Lifespan in Mice
hypotheses.claim: Administration of oridonin extends lifespan in Mus musculus. The compound increases median and maximum lifespan relative to untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Oridonin modulates inflammatory and proteostasis pathways that govern aging rate. Suppressing chronic inflammation can preserve tissue function and delay mortality.
hypotheses.prediction: Oridonin-treated mice will show significantly longer median and maximum lifespan than vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a large cohort of age-matched mice to oridonin or vehicle, maintain treatment for life, and compare survival curves with log-rank analysis.

hypotheses.title: Alpha-Lipoic Acid Extends Lifespan in Mice
hypotheses.claim: Administration of alpha-lipoic acid extends lifespan in Mus musculus. The compound increases median and maximum lifespan relative to untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Alpha-lipoic acid is a mitochondrial cofactor and antioxidant that can reduce oxidative damage. Lowering accumulated damage may slow functional decline and extend survival.
hypotheses.prediction: Alpha-lipoic acid-treated mice will show significantly longer median and maximum lifespan than vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a large cohort of age-matched mice to alpha-lipoic acid or vehicle, maintain treatment for life, and compare survival curves with log-rank analysis.

hypotheses.title: Spermidine Extends Lifespan in Mice via Sirtuin Activation
hypotheses.claim: Spermidine extends lifespan in Mus musculus by directly activating sirtuins. The lifespan increase depends on sirtuin activity and is abolished when sirtuins are inactive.
hypotheses.rationale: Sirtuins regulate stress resistance, metabolism, and chromatin maintenance in ways that influence aging. Direct activation of these enzymes could coordinately improve tissue maintenance and extend survival.
hypotheses.prediction: Spermidine will extend lifespan in control mice but not in mice with genetically or pharmacologically inactivated sirtuins.
hypotheses.experiment: Treat wild-type and sirtuin-deficient mice with spermidine or vehicle for life and compare survival curves across all four groups.

hypotheses.title: Oridonin Extends Lifespan in Mice via mTOR Activation
hypotheses.claim: Oridonin extends lifespan in Mus musculus by activating mTOR signaling. The lifespan increase requires mTOR activation and is lost when mTOR signaling is blocked.
hypotheses.rationale: mTOR signaling governs growth, autophagy, and cellular metabolism, and its activity state can shape aging trajectories. Activation under specific conditions may enhance repair and maintenance processes that extend survival.
hypotheses.prediction: Oridonin will extend lifespan in control mice but not in mice treated with mTOR inhibitors or carrying reduced mTOR activity.
hypotheses.experiment: Treat mice with oridonin plus vehicle, oridonin plus an mTOR inhibitor, or vehicle alone for life and compare survival curves across groups.

hypotheses.title: Prednisolone Sodium Phosphate Extends Lifespan in Mice
hypotheses.claim: Administration of prednisolone sodium phosphate extends lifespan in Mus musculus. The compound increases median and maximum lifespan relative to untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Glucocorticoids potently suppress inflammation, a driver of age-related tissue deterioration. Sustained anti-inflammatory signaling could preserve organ function and prolong survival.
hypotheses.prediction: Prednisolone sodium phosphate-treated mice will show significantly longer median and maximum lifespan than vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a large cohort of age-matched mice to prednisolone sodium phosphate or vehicle, maintain treatment for life, and compare survival curves with log-rank analysis.

hypotheses.title: Putrescine Extends Lifespan in Mice
hypotheses.claim: Administration of putrescine extends lifespan in Mus musculus. The compound increases median and maximum lifespan relative to untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Putrescine is a natural polyamine involved in growth, membrane stability, and autophagy regulation. Maintaining polyamine pools during aging can support cellular renewal and extend survival.
hypotheses.prediction: Putrescine-treated mice will show significantly longer median and maximum lifespan than vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a large cohort of age-matched mice to putrescine or vehicle, maintain treatment for life, and compare survival curves with log-rank analysis.

hypotheses.title: Spermidine Extends Lifespan in Mice
hypotheses.claim: Administration of spermidine extends lifespan in Mus musculus. The compound increases median and maximum lifespan relative to untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Spermidine induces autophagy and supports proteostasis, both of which decline with age. Restoring autophagic flux can slow cellular deterioration and extend survival.
hypotheses.prediction: Spermidine-treated mice will show significantly longer median and maximum lifespan than vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a large cohort of age-matched mice to spermidine or vehicle, maintain treatment for life, and compare survival curves with log-rank analysis.

hypotheses.title: Oridonin Shortens Lifespan in Mice
hypotheses.claim: Administration of oridonin shortens lifespan in Mus musculus. The compound decreases median and maximum lifespan relative to untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Oridonin is a bioactive diterpenoid with cytotoxic and stress-inducing properties. Chronic exposure to such stressors can damage tissues and accelerate mortality.
hypotheses.prediction: Oridonin-treated mice will show significantly shorter median and maximum lifespan than vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a large cohort of age-matched mice to oridonin or vehicle, maintain treatment for life, and compare survival curves with log-rank analysis.

hypotheses.title: Spermidine in Drinking Water Shortens Lifespan in Mice
hypotheses.claim: Spermidine shortens lifespan in Mus musculus when administered in drinking water. This route of delivery decreases median and maximum lifespan relative to untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Drinking-water delivery produces continuous exposure that may exceed beneficial polyamine levels. Chronic excess can disrupt polyamine homeostasis and metabolism in ways that accelerate mortality.
hypotheses.prediction: Mice receiving spermidine in drinking water will show significantly shorter median and maximum lifespan than vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a large cohort of age-matched mice to spermidine in drinking water or plain water, maintain treatment for life, and compare survival curves with log-rank analysis.
